intent.notes: Lunch-break session at a weights gym, about 55 min: shoulders (overhead press 4x8, lateral raise 4x12), triceps 4x10 and biceps 4x8, then floor core (side plank, hollow hold) and handstand practice last. The handstand closes the session on purpose: it needs a free wall and room around it, and by the end of the lunch hour the crowd has usually thinned out. By then shoulders and triceps are already worked, so it stays practice and never a set to failure: both drills are chest to the wall, keep every hold well short of failure and come down as soon as the elbows soften or the shoulders sink, while you can still walk the feet down under control. Loaded lifts at RIR 1-2 (one or two clean reps left in the tank); loads come from your working loads and move with your feedback. For a dumbbell exercise the load is per dumbbell (one hand). No finger load, no hanging, no heavy pull. The curl is elbow-flexor work: keep it away from the 24 h before a heavy pulling session. The four lifts appear in the engine's generic order: any order among them works, and the overhead press can go first if you want your best numbers on it. After the lifts the floor core and the toe pulls follow the same generic order, and the wall handstand hold is always the last exercise. In a deload week the app already drops one set from every lift and floor core exercise (the handstand practice keeps its sets): stop every lift at RIR 3.

modules.notes: Short pulse raise before the lifts.

prescription_overrides.notes: 2 min of light jogging in place or easy cardio, with arm swings.

modules.notes: Thoracic and shoulder mobility plus wrist preparation: the wrists carry the whole body in the handstand.

prescription_overrides.notes: 2 min of thoracic rotations, arm circles and scapular circles, then 1 min of wrist prep on the floor: wrist circles, rock forward and back on flat palms with the fingers pointing forward, then backward. No static stretching.

modules.notes: Balance practice at the end of the session: toe pulls from a chest-to-wall handstand, the bridge to a freestanding handstand. The shoulders are already worked: stop well before failure.

prescription_overrides.notes: Wrists first: 30 s of rocks on flat palms, fingers forward then backward (the warm-up was about 40 min ago). Then 3 x 3 attempts: walk up chest to the wall (only the toes touch it), pull the toes of one foot off, then the other, and hunt for the balance line for a few seconds. Correct with finger pressure, not with the shoulders. The shoulders are tired from the lifts: stop the set when the line gets sloppy or the elbows soften. This is practice, not a set to failure.

modules.notes: Chest-to-wall handstand hold, always the last exercise of the session: the foundation of every other handstand drill, and the measurable target of this block (a clean 30 s hold also opens the next level of the vertical-push ladder).

prescription_overrides.notes: If the toe pulls were skipped, start with 30 s of wrist rocks on flat palms. Target: 4 x 30 s clean, belly to the wall, hands 15-20 cm from it. Push the floor away, ribs closed, glutes tight. Walk the feet down as soon as the shoulders sink, the elbows soften or the back arches, while you can still do it under control: after the lifts a clean shorter hold is worth more than a sagging 30 s. Log the seconds of your weakest hold.

modules.notes: Vertical press for the shoulders, the heaviest lift of the session: the app may list it after the curl and the lateral raise, do it first of the four lifts if you want your best numbers on it. The same movement every time so the load can progress from feedback.

prescription_overrides.notes: 4 x 8 at RIR 1-2, seated dumbbell press or standing barbell, always the same implement. With dumbbells the load is per dumbbell. 3 s lowering phase, ribs down. If every set felt like RIR 3 or more, log the session as easy and the next load goes up.

modules.notes: Lateral raise for the side of the shoulder, which climbing barely trains.

prescription_overrides.notes: 4 x 12 at RIR 1-2, load per dumbbell. Lead with the elbows up to shoulder height, never above, 2-3 s down.

modules.notes: Triceps in the stretched position: an overhead extension with one dumbbell, so the long head works where the cable pushdown of the push lunch does not reach.

prescription_overrides.notes: 4 x 10 at RIR 1-2 with one dumbbell held in both hands: the load is that one dumbbell. Elbows in, ribs down, full stretch behind the head. If every set felt like RIR 3 or more, log it as easy and the load goes up.

modules.notes: Elbow flexion with a neutral grip: the hammer curl puts the brachialis and brachioradialis to work, the flexors that hold a lock-off (the push lunch has the supinated curl). Never a weighted pull-up or chin-up.

prescription_overrides.notes: 4 x 8 at RIR 1-2, load per dumbbell, thumbs up, elbows pinned, 3 s lowering phase, no swing. If every set felt like RIR 3 or more, log it as easy and the load goes up.

modules.notes: Floor core, lateral chain: side plank on the forearm; a tested athlete gets his lateral ladder level instead (Copenhagen). No hanging, no front lever.

prescription_overrides.notes: 3 x 30 s per side, elbow under the shoulder, hips high in one line from head to feet.

modules.notes: Floor core before the handstand hold: hollow hold, the line the handstand needs; a tested athlete gets his L-sit or rollout ladder level instead (else his hollow ladder). No hanging, no front lever.

prescription_overrides.notes: 3 x 30 s hollow hold: lower back pressed to the floor, arms by the ears, heels a hand off the floor. Shorten the lever (knees bent) before the back lifts.
